children: A LOT OF BEARS IN THIS ZOO
The AI shakeout has caused volatile shifts in many tech-related stocks, and more than half the stocks in the Nasdaq 100
are now in a bear market, according to a note from SentimenTrader on Tuesday.

The firm notes that as investors begin to avoid risk, technology and other growth companies can come under pressure sooner than the overall market, and even when the overall indexes are not showing much of a decline, a large portion of individual stocks within them can already be well below their highs.
As of November 16, 54% of the Nasdaq 100 components were 20% below their 52-week highs, while only 32% of the S&P 500
With that many stocks showing sharp declines, it could be a "clear warning," but on the other hand, it could mean a strong rebound is possible.

SentimenTrader said that historically, similar instances of more than half the Nasdaq 100 being in a bear market have led into sustained bear markets, but have also marked the start of strong rebounds.

But more telling, according to the firm, is that the weakness in growth stocks has already run further than in the S&P 500, and "when that gap has widened to a similar degree, the S&P 500 has historically done poorly over the following one to three months, with deeper drawdowns along the way."

As for what it all means for the current market, the firm said it leans toward caution in the benchmark S&P index over the next few months, noting that "whether the S&P 500's own bear-market share catches up to the Nasdaq's, or whether the Nasdaq repairs more broadly first," is the key thing to watch.
